scope: Native Firestore avatar admission, upload lease, original receipt, replacement and maintenance cleanup; not a full restore or HTTP deployment

environment.clients: Two independent Firestore SDK clients in one process, then a reconstructed client

indexes.changes: Two existing composite definitions under the isolated namespace, private field exclusions, and cleanup.complete ascending index

assertions: Concurrent reservations share the pending cap; third reservation rejected and original opId returns the same reservation
Persisted processing lease prevents a second store admitting the same in-flight upload
Formal online submission commits version 1 once; receipt replay returns the same asset
An unknown user cannot read the image
Replacement commits version 2 and invalidates old content access
Formal maintenance, background queue and cleanup consumer remove superseded content
Duplicate worker delivery returns completed without another object removal
A reconstructed SDK client reads the same current head and encrypted content
transport: External Cloud Tasks enqueue replaced by a local inbox; one wake passed to the real queue and maintenance consumer
cleanup: Both written synthetic images removed at pinned generations and synthetic product account revoked. Encrypted authority, receipts and cleanup rows retained. No Firebase Auth account or deletion journal entry created.
review: Main-model source review plus independent read-only harness review. Fixed barrier failure handling, cleanup handles and full namespace absence checks before the single execution.

costs.actualBill: Not measured; bounded SDK calls on existing synthetic resources

limitations: Same-process SDK clients are not two deployed API replicas
No Cloud Tasks/OIDC dispatch, HTTP routing or production deployment verification
No explicit avatar removal journal, account export, paired backup or full isolated restore
No device crop/EXIF verification; release gate remains false
Storage soft-delete policy unchanged; absence of a live generation does not prove immediate physical erasure
